objects.definition: typedef unsigned long long int gdbm_count_t;
objects.description: Typedef for an unsigned 64-bit counter used by GDBM for record and bucket counts.
Key/value blob used by GDBM and NDBM APIs. dptr points to a memory buffer of length dsize bytes. Caller generally manages allocation and lifetime unless otherwise documented by specific API calls.
Opaque handle to an open GDBM database. It is a typedef to a pointer to an internal struct gdbm_file_info, whose definition is not exposed in this header.

objects.definition:
struct gdbm_open_spec
{
  int fd;              /* Unless -1, this is the handle of an already opened
			  database file.  gdbm_open_ext will use it instead
			  of opening the named file with open(2). */
  int mode;            /* File mode in case it will be created. */
  int block_size;      /* Block size to use when creating new file.  0 stands
			  for default. */
  int lock_wait;       /* Whether and how to wait for database lock to
			  succeed.  GDBM_LOCKWAIT_NONE means return
			  immediately, if the database cannot be locked.
			  Otherwise, block until the file is locked or
			  timeout expires. */
  struct timespec lock_timeout;  /* Locking timeout. */
  struct timespec lock_interval; /* For GDBM_LOCKWAIT_RETRY, interval to
				    sleep between two successive locking
				    attempts. */

  void (*fatal_func) (const char *); /* Function to call before returning
					fatal error. Deprecated. */
};
objects.description: Specifies extended parameters for opening a GDBM database via gdbm_open_ext, including existing fd, mode, block size, locking behavior, timeouts, and an optional deprecated fatal handler.
Configuration and result carrier for database recovery via gdbm_recover. Input fields control limits and error reporting; output fields report recovery results and optional backup file name.
Integer typedef representing GDBM-specific error codes. Values correspond to the GDBM_* constants defined in this header.
Per-bucket cache statistic entry used with gdbm_get_cache_stats to report address and hit count.
Opaque-like handle for the NDBM compatibility API layered over GDBM. Holds the underlying GDBM_FILE and related state for .dir/.pag files, last-returned key/value memory, and last error code.
Enumerates status codes returned by snapshot selection helpers, indicating success, error, or suspicious results.

functions.name: gdbm_open_spec_init
functions.description: Initializes a gdbm_open_spec structure to default values before use with gdbm_open_ext. Use this to ensure all fields are in a known state (a documented initializer macro also exists).
requirements: spec must be a valid, writable pointer to a struct gdbm_open_spec.
Call this before passing the struct to gdbm_open_ext, unless you use GDBM_OPEN_SPEC_INITIALIZER.
The function does not allocate memory; the caller owns the struct storage.

functions.name: gdbm_open_ext
functions.signature: GDBM_FILE gdbm_open_ext (char const *file_name, int flags, struct gdbm_open_spec const *op);
functions.description: Opens a GDBM database using extended parameters supplied via gdbm_open_spec (e.g., file descriptor reuse, lock behavior, block size). Returns an opaque GDBM_FILE handle on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: file_name must point to a valid null-terminated path string when op->fd == -1.
op must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized gdbm_open_spec (initialize via gdbm_open_spec_init or GDBM_OPEN_SPEC_INITIALIZER).

flags must be a combination of GDBM_READER/GDBM_WRITER/GDBM_WRCREAT/GDBM_NEWDB (masked by GDBM_OPENMASK) and may include additional GDBM_* open flags (e.g., GDBM_SYNC, GDBM_NOLOCK, GDBM_NOMMAP, GDBM_CLOEXEC, GDBM_BSEXACT, GDBM_CLOERROR, GDBM_XVERIFY, GDBM_PREREAD, GDBM_NUMSYNC).
If op->fd != -1, it must be a valid open file descriptor for the database file.
On failure, inspect errno/gdbm_errno via library helpers (details of error reporting are not specified in this header).

functions.name: gdbm_fd_open
functions.signature: GDBM_FILE gdbm_fd_open (int fd, const char *file_name, int block_size, int flags, void (*fatal_func) (const char *));
functions.description: Associates an already-open file descriptor with a new GDBM database handle. Allows specifying block size and open flags similar to gdbm_open. Returns a GDBM_FILE or NULL on failure.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor referring to the target database file.
file_name must be a valid path string associated with fd (used by the library; exact use not specified).
block_size is the desired database block size when creating a new database; semantics of 0 or constraints are not specified here.
flags must use GDBM_READER/WRITER/WRCREAT/NEWDB (GDBM_OPENMASK) and may include additional GDBM_* open flags documented in this header.
If GDBM_CLOERROR is used, the fd may be closed by the library on error (per header comment for that flag).
fatal_func is a callback invoked on fatal error (deprecated per gdbm_open_spec); it may be NULL (not specified here; unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_open
functions.signature: GDBM_FILE gdbm_open (const char *, int, int, int, void (*)(const char *));
functions.description: Opens a GDBM database with basic parameters: filename, block size, flags, mode, and optional fatal callback. Returns a GDBM_FILE handle or NULL on error.
requirements: The first argument must be a valid null-terminated filename string.
The second argument is the block size; constraints are not specified here (unknown).
The third argument is flags (GDBM_READER/WRITER/WRCREAT/NEWDB with possible extra GDBM_* open flags).
The fourth argument is file mode used when creating a file (typical Unix permission mask).
The last argument is an optional fatal error callback (deprecated; may be NULL—behavior not specified in this header; unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_close
functions.description: Closes a previously opened GDBM database handle and releases associated resources.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE argument must be a valid handle obtained from a successful gdbm_open/gdbm_fd_open/gdbm_open_ext call and not already closed.
After this call, the handle must not be used.

functions.name: gdbm_store
functions.description: Inserts or replaces a key/value pair in the database. Use flags GDBM_INSERT to avoid overwriting or GDBM_REPLACE to overwrite existing data.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be opened for writing (not a reader).
The key and content datum parameters must be initialized: dptr must point to a buffer of at least dsize bytes (dsize may be 0; whether zero-length keys are allowed is not specified here—unknown).
The flags argument must be either GDBM_INSERT or GDBM_REPLACE.
Caller must check the return value to determine success or failure; exact conventions are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_fetch
functions.description: Looks up a key and returns the associated value as a datum. On failure or missing key, the returned datum contents and ownership semantics are not specified in this header.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open database handle.
The key datum must be initialized with dptr pointing to a buffer of length dsize.
Caller must handle the case where the key is not found; exact indicator (e.g., NULL dptr) and memory ownership for the returned datum are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_delete
functions.description: Deletes a record with the specified key from the database.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be open for writing.
The key datum must be initialized (dptr valid for dsize bytes).
Caller must check the return value for success or failure; exact return codes are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_firstkey
functions.description: Returns the first key in the database iteration order. Typically used with gdbm_nextkey to iterate over all keys. Allocation/ownership of the returned datum is not specified in this header.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open database handle.
Caller should be prepared for the case of an empty database; the indicator and memory ownership for the returned datum are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_nextkey
functions.description: Returns the next key following the given key to support iteration over database keys. The iteration semantics and memory ownership of the returned datum are not specified in this header.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open database handle.
The input key datum must be initialized and typically be a previously seen key from gdbm_firstkey/gdbm_nextkey (exact requirements not specified—unknown).
Caller must handle end-of-iteration; indicator and memory ownership are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_reorganize
functions.description: Reorganizes the database file to reclaim space and improve layout. Intended for maintenance operations.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be open for writing.
Caller should ensure no concurrent writers not coordinated by GDBM locking (concurrency details not specified here—unknown).
Check the return value for success or failure; exact codes are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_sync
functions.description: Forces any cached changes to be synchronized to disk (fsync-like).
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open database handle (typically with write access if changes exist).
Check the return value for success/failure; exact codes are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_failure_atomic
functions.signature: int gdbm_failure_atomic (GDBM_FILE, const char *, const char *);
functions.description: Performs operations related to failure-atomic behavior for the database (exact semantics are not documented in this header). Likely used to ensure consistency around critical operations.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open handle.
The two const char* parameters must be valid strings; their meanings are not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check the return value; success/failure conventions are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_convert
functions.description: Converts the database to another on-disk format or version (purpose inferred from name; exact conversion modes and effects are not documented in this header).
requirements: dbf must be a valid, open GDBM_FILE.
flag controls conversion behavior; accepted values are not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check return value to detect errors (unknown conventions).

functions.name: gdbm_latest_snapshot
functions.signature: int gdbm_latest_snapshot (const char *, const char *, const char **);
functions.description: Selects the latest usable snapshot among two candidates and optionally reports which one. Return codes are defined by enum gdbm_latest_snapshot_status.
requirements: The first two const char* arguments must be valid path strings to candidate snapshot files (semantics inferred from name and enum).
The third argument must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the selected snapshot path or indicator (exact output semantics are not specified here).
Caller must interpret the return value using gdbm_latest_snapshot_status constants.

functions.name: gdbm_exists
functions.description: Checks whether a key exists in the database.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open handle.
The key datum must be initialized (dptr valid for dsize bytes).
Caller must check the integer return value; specific success/failure/boolean conventions are not defined in this header (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_setopt
functions.description: Gets or sets database options depending on the option code. Supports both setters and getters as indicated by GDBM_SET*/GDBM_GET* constants.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open handle.
The option code must be one of the defined GDBM_SETCACHESIZE/SETSYNCMODE/etc. or GDBM_GET* codes in this header.
The value pointer must point to a buffer of the appropriate type/size for the option, and the integer size argument must be the size in bytes of the data pointed to by the value pointer.
For setters, the pointed-to value must be initialized; for getters, the buffer must be writable.
Caller must check the return value for success/failure; exact codes are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_fdesc
functions.description: Returns the underlying file descriptor associated with a GDBM database handle.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open handle.
Caller must handle negative return values as errors (exact conventions not specified here—unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_export
functions.signature: int gdbm_export (GDBM_FILE, const char *, int, int);
functions.description: Exports the database to a file by path in a specified dump format and with given open flags for the output file.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open handle (read access sufficient).
The path must be a valid, writable filename string.
The third argument fmt must be a supported dump format: GDBM_DUMP_FMT_BINARY or GDBM_DUMP_FMT_ASCII.
The fourth argument open_flags should be appropriate flags/mode for creating the output file (exact semantics not specified here—unknown).
Caller must check the return value for errors (unknown conventions).

functions.name: gdbm_export_to_file
functions.description: Exports the database to an already opened FILE stream in the library’s default export format.
requirements: dbf must be a valid, open GDBM_FILE.
fp must be a valid, writable FILE* opened by the caller.
Caller must check the return value for errors (unknown conventions).

functions.name: gdbm_import
functions.description: Imports database contents from a dump file specified by path. The flag controls behavior (e.g., replace or merge; exact options not documented here).
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open handle, typically opened for writing.
The path must be a valid, readable filename string.
The flag parameter controls import behavior; accepted values are not specified in this header (unknown).
Caller must check the return value for success/failure (unknown conventions).

functions.name: gdbm_import_from_file
functions.signature: int gdbm_import_from_file (GDBM_FILE dbf, FILE *fp, int flag);
functions.description: Imports database contents from an already-open FILE stream. The flag controls import behavior (undocumented here).
requirements: dbf must be a valid, open GDBM_FILE (typically writable).
fp must be a valid, readable FILE*.
flag controls behavior; accepted values not specified here (unknown).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: gdbm_count
functions.description: Counts the number of key/value records in the database and stores it in pcount.
requirements: dbf must be a valid, open GDBM_FILE.
pcount must be a non-NULL pointer to gdbm_count_t where the result will be stored.
Caller must check the integer return value to detect errors (unknown conventions).

functions.name: gdbm_bucket_count
functions.description: Returns the number of hash buckets in the database’s internal structure and stores it in pcount.
requirements: dbf must be a valid, open GDBM_FILE.
pcount must be a non-NULL pointer to size_t.
Caller must check the integer return value to detect errors (unknown conventions).

functions.name: gdbm_avail_verify
functions.description: Verifies the internal free-space (availability) structures of the database for consistency. Intended for diagnostics/maintenance.
requirements: dbf must be a valid, open GDBM_FILE.
Caller must check the return value for errors; exact codes are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_recover
functions.signature: int gdbm_recover (GDBM_FILE dbf, gdbm_recovery *rcvr, int flags);
functions.description: Attempts to recover a damaged database. The rcvr structure provides input limits and receives detailed recovery statistics and optional backup name. The flags indicate which rcvr fields are initialized and control recovery behavior.
requirements: dbf must be a valid, open GDBM_FILE.

rcvr must be a valid pointer to a gdbm_recovery struct; input members must be initialized according to flags set (e.g., GDBM_RCVR_ERRFUN, GDBM_RCVR_MAX_FAILED_KEYS, GDBM_RCVR_MAX_FAILED_BUCKETS, GDBM_RCVR_MAX_FAILURES).
If GDBM_RCVR_BACKUP is set, the library will keep a backup copy of the original database on success (per comment).
If GDBM_RCVR_FORCE is set, recovery will skip the check pass (per comment).
Caller must check the return value; detailed semantics are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_dump
functions.signature: int gdbm_dump (GDBM_FILE, const char *, int fmt, int open_flags, int mode);
functions.description: Dumps the database to a file at the given path using the specified format, open flags, and file mode for creation.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open handle (read access sufficient).
The path must be a valid writable filename string.
fmt must be one of GDBM_DUMP_FMT_BINARY or GDBM_DUMP_FMT_ASCII.
open_flags and mode must be appropriate for creating/opening the output file (semantics not documented here—unknown).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: gdbm_dump_to_file
functions.description: Dumps the database to an already-open stream using the specified format.
requirements: The GDBM_FILE must be a valid, open handle.
The FILE* must be a valid, writable stream.
fmt must be one of GDBM_DUMP_FMT_BINARY or GDBM_DUMP_FMT_ASCII.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: gdbm_load
functions.signature: int gdbm_load (GDBM_FILE *, const char *, int replace, int meta_flags, unsigned long *line);
functions.description: Creates/opens and loads a database from a dump file at the given path, optionally replacing existing records and restoring metadata per flags. On return, the GDBM_FILE* may be updated to the opened database. Tracks progress line number.
requirements: The first argument must be a non-NULL pointer to a GDBM_FILE handle variable that the function may set.
The path must be a valid, readable filename string.
replace controls whether to replace existing records; flag values are not specified here (unknown).
meta_flags controls which metadata to restore; see GDBM_META_MASK_MODE and GDBM_META_MASK_OWNER.
line, if non-NULL, points to an unsigned long to receive a line counter; whether NULL is allowed is not specified (unknown).
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: gdbm_load_from_file
functions.signature: int gdbm_load_from_file (GDBM_FILE *, FILE *, int replace, int meta_flags, unsigned long *line);
functions.description: Loads a database from an already-open FILE stream, with options to replace and restore selected metadata. May open/create the database and set the provided GDBM_FILE*.
requirements: The first argument must be a non-NULL pointer to a GDBM_FILE handle variable.
The FILE* must be a valid, readable stream positioned at the beginning of a GDBM dump.
replace flag usage is as in gdbm_load (not documented here).
meta_flags uses GDBM_META_MASK_* bits as in gdbm_load.
line may be used to receive a line number; details not specified.
Caller must check the return value for errors.

functions.name: gdbm_load_from_file_ext
functions.signature: int gdbm_load_from_file_ext (GDBM_FILE *pdbf, FILE *fp, int mode, int replace, int meta_mask, unsigned long *line);
functions.description: Extended loader variant that accepts a file creation mode, replace flag, and a metadata mask for selective restoration, reading from an existing FILE stream.
requirements: pdbf must be a non-NULL pointer to a GDBM_FILE handle variable.
fp must be a valid, readable FILE*.
mode is a file mode used for database creation; exact semantics not detailed here.
replace controls overwrite behavior; values not documented.
meta_mask selects which metadata to restore; use GDBM_META_MASK_* bits.
line may be used to receive a progress counter; details unknown.
Caller must check return value for errors.

functions.name: gdbm_copy_meta
functions.description: Copies metadata (e.g., mode/owner as controlled by related APIs) from src database to dst database.
requirements: dst and src must be valid, open GDBM_FILE handles.
Caller must ensure appropriate permissions to set metadata on dst (system-dependent; not specified here).
Check the return value for success/failure.

functions.name: gdbm_errno_location
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the thread-local/global gdbm_errno variable used by the library for error reporting.
requirements: No arguments. The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.
Caller may read or assign through the returned pointer; semantics of direct modification are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_last_errno
functions.description: Returns the last GDBM-specific error code associated with the given database handle.
requirements: dbf must be a valid GDBM_FILE handle.
Caller uses the returned gdbm_error to interpret the last error; mapping to system errno is via gdbm_last_syserr/gdbm_syserr.

functions.name: gdbm_last_syserr
functions.description: Returns the last underlying system errno value associated with the given database handle.
requirements: dbf must be a valid GDBM_FILE handle.
Caller interprets 0/non-0 according to library conventions (not documented here).

functions.name: gdbm_set_errno
functions.signature: void gdbm_set_errno (GDBM_FILE dbf, gdbm_error ec, int fatal);
functions.description: Sets the GDBM-specific error code for a database handle and indicates whether it is fatal.
requirements: dbf must be a valid GDBM_FILE handle (may be NULL for global error—not specified here; unknown).
ec must be a valid gdbm_error code (see enum in header).
fatal is a flag; exact non-zero/zero semantics are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_clear_error
functions.description: Clears the recorded error state for the database handle.
requirements: dbf must be a valid GDBM_FILE handle.

functions.name: gdbm_needs_recovery
functions.description: Checks whether the database requires recovery before normal use.
requirements: dbf must be a valid GDBM_FILE handle.
Caller must inspect the integer return value; exact conventions are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_check_syserr
functions.description: Utility to check if a GDBM error code implies a system errno is also set, based on library mapping.
requirements: n must be a valid gdbm_error value.
Caller must inspect the integer return; exact conventions are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the given GDBM error code.
requirements: Argument must be a valid gdbm_error code.
Returned string is owned by the library; do not modify or free.

functions.name: gdbm_db_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the last error for the given database handle.
requirements: dbf must be a valid GDBM_FILE handle.
Returned string is library-owned; do not modify or free.

functions.name: gdbm_version_cmp
functions.signature: int gdbm_version_cmp (int const a[], int const b[]);
functions.description: Compares two version arrays [major, minor, patch]. Returns ordering information as an integer (exact convention is typical strcmp-like but not specified here).
requirements: a and b must each point to arrays of at least 3 integers: {major, minor, patch}.
Caller interprets the return value according to library documentation (not specified here—unknown).

functions.name: gdbm_get_cache_stats
functions.signature: void gdbm_get_cache_stats (GDBM_FILE dbf, size_t *access_count, size_t *cache_hits, size_t *cache_count, struct gdbm_cache_stat *bstat, size_t nstat);
functions.description: Retrieves cache usage statistics for the database, including aggregate counts and per-bucket stats into an array of gdbm_cache_stat of length nstat.
requirements: dbf must be a valid, open GDBM_FILE.
Any non-NULL counter pointers (access_count, cache_hits, cache_count) must point to writable size_t locations; pass NULL to skip a counter (not specified but typical—unknown).
If bstat is non-NULL, it must point to an array of at least nstat elements; if nstat is 0, bstat may be NULL (not specified here—unknown).

functions.name: dbm_open
functions.description: Opens an NDBM-compatible database (wrapper over GDBM) using the given path, flags, and mode. Returns a DBM* handle or NULL on error.
requirements: file must be a valid null-terminated filename string (without extension handling specified here).
flags and mode are used to open/create the database; specific flag semantics follow GDBM open flags (not detailed here).
Caller must check for NULL return to detect errors.

functions.name: dbm_close
functions.description: Closes an NDBM database handle and releases associated resources.
requirements: dbf must be a valid pointer returned by dbm_open and not yet closed.
After closing, dbf must not be used.

functions.name: dbm_fetch
functions.description: Fetches the value associated with key from an NDBM database. Returns a datum; ownership/validity semantics are not specified here.
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle.
key must be an initialized datum (dptr valid for dsize bytes).
Caller must handle not-found cases and any memory management as defined by the implementation (not specified here—unknown).

functions.name: dbm_store
functions.signature: int dbm_store (DBM *dbf, datum key, datum content, int flags);
functions.description: Inserts or replaces a key/value pair in an NDBM database. Use DBM_INSERT or DBM_REPLACE for the flags.
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle opened for writing.
key and content must be initialized datums with valid buffers.
flags must be DBM_INSERT or DBM_REPLACE.
Caller must check the integer return value to detect errors; exact conventions are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: dbm_delete
functions.description: Deletes the record identified by key from an NDBM database.
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle opened for writing.
key must be an initialized datum (dptr valid for dsize bytes).
Caller must check the return value for success/failure (unknown conventions).

functions.name: dbm_firstkey
functions.description: Returns the first key in the NDBM database to begin iteration. Ownership/validity semantics of the returned datum are not specified here.
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle.
Caller must handle empty database case; indicator and memory ownership are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: dbm_nextkey
functions.description: Returns the next key in the NDBM database iteration. Use repeatedly after dbm_firstkey to iterate keys. Ownership/validity semantics are not specified here.
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle.
Caller must detect end-of-iteration; indicator and ownership are not specified here (unknown).

functions.name: dbm_error
functions.description: Returns the last error code recorded for the DBM handle (wrapper over GDBM error reporting).
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle.
Caller interprets nonzero/zero according to implementation (not specified here—unknown).

functions.name: dbm_clearerr
functions.description: Clears the error state for the DBM handle.
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle.

functions.name: dbm_dirfno
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor of the .dir file associated with the NDBM database.
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle.
Caller must handle negative return values as errors (conventions not specified—unknown).

functions.name: dbm_pagfno
functions.description: Returns the file descriptor of the .pag file associated with the NDBM database (backed by GDBM_FILE).
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle.
Caller must handle negative return values as errors (unknown conventions).

functions.name: dbm_rdonly
functions.description: Indicates whether the database was opened read-only.
requirements: dbf must be a valid DBM* handle.
Caller interprets the integer return per implementation (nonzero for read-only is typical but not specified here—unknown).

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces bytes representing a valid, null-terminated filesystem path string.
# It targets stubs that call FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() for operations such as:
# - gdbm_open/gdbm_open_ext/gdbm_fd_open: need writable locations (creation) or readable paths
# - gdbm_dump/export (output files): need parent dirs to exist
# - gdbm_import/load (input files): need readable dump-like files; but we only provide a path string,
#   the fuzzer harness will populate file contents with its own data. Our duty is to return a path
#   that the harness considers valid and can open relative to its working directory.
# Strategy:
# - Return a single NUL-terminated C string path (bytes) suitable for POSIX-like environments.
# - Mix of relative and simple nested directories to diversify behavior.
# - Avoid characters that are often disallowed on Windows (keep cross-platform-ish), but include
#   spaces and dots which are commonly handled.
# - Ensure total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Occasionally include different file extensions relevant to GDBM use: .gdbm, .dump, .dir, .pag
# - Optionally include a second path separated by a newline to seed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME calls
#   in a single buffer; the harness typically pulls sequentially from the same input. However, some
#   fuzzers map each FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME to the next slice. To keep compatibility, we place multiple
#   NUL-terminated strings back-to-back so each call can read the next C-string.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

EXTS = [
    ".gdbm",
    ".db",
    ".dump",
    ".txt",
    ".bin",
    ".dir",
    ".pag",
    "",
]

DIR_PREFIXES = [
    ".",  # current directory
    "./out",
    "./tmp",
    "./data",
    "./var",
    "./snapshots",
]

BASENAMES = [
    "db",
    "test",
    "store",
    "gdbm",
    "snapshot",
    "input",
    "output",
    "dump",
]


def _rand_component(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 3, max_len: int = 12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid trailing/leading spaces entirely to reduce platform quirks
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    return s


def _rand_basename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base = rng.choice(BASENAMES)
    else:
        base = _rand_component(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # add an extra token to create names like db_001 or store-alpha
        sep = rng.choice(["-", "_", " "])
        base += sep + _rand_component(rng, 1, 6)
    return base


def _rand_ext(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(EXTS)


def _rand_dirpath(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build 0-3 nested components under a chosen prefix
    prefix = rng.choice(DIR_PREFIXES)
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    parts: List[str] = [prefix]
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_component(rng, 2, 8))
    return "/".join(parts)


def _rand_rel_or_abs(rng: random.Random) -> bool:
    # Favor relative paths for harness sandboxes
    return rng.random() < 0.85


def _build_path(rng: random.Random, want_dir: bool = False) -> str:
    # Construct a path to a file (or directory if want_dir)
    if _rand_rel_or_abs(rng):
        dirpath = _rand_dirpath(rng)
    else:
        # absolute path under a generic root to remain sandbox-safe
        # Use /tmp-like area
        root = rng.choice(["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/tmp/fuzz"])  # POSIX style
        extra = "" if rng.random() < 0.3 else "/" + _rand_component(rng, 2, 8)
        dirpath = root + extra
    if want_dir:
        return dirpath
    fname = _rand_basename(rng) + _rand_ext(rng)
    return dirpath.rstrip("/") + "/" + fname


def _multi_paths_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Many stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME multiple times; provide 2-4 paths back-to-back.
    n = rng.randint(2, 4)
    paths: List[str] = []
    # Mix files that could serve as inputs and outputs
    for i in range(n):
        if i == 0 and rng.random() < 0.3:
            # Sometimes offer a directory path as first, though most APIs expect files.
            p = _build_path(rng, want_dir=True)
        else:
            p = _build_path(rng, want_dir=False)
        # Normalize double slashes and ensure not exceeding length
        p = p.replace('//', '/').rstrip()
        if not p:
            p = "./x"
        paths.append(p)
    # NUL-terminate each C string and concatenate
    out = bytearray()
    for p in paths:
        b = p.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')[:1023]  # keep each path short
        out += b + b"\x00"
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    buf = _multi_paths_buffer(rng)
    # Ensure total size limit
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4095] + b"\x00"
    # As a final guarantee, include at least one standalone path if buffer ended empty
    if not buf:
        single = _build_path(rng)
        return single.encode('utf-8') + b"\x00"
    return buf

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for GDBM/NDBM datum-friendly binary blobs, intended to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# - Produces valid, interesting keys/values as arbitrary binary blobs (including NULs).
# - Respects fuzzer stub size caps: key <= 256, value <= 512.
# - Covers edge cases (empty, max size, repeated bytes, ASCII text, UTF-8, random, structured).
# - Returns a single bytes buffer of length <= 4096, composed of length-prefixed entries
#   so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can be consumed sequentially.
# Entry format: 2-byte big-endian length (L), then L bytes payload.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_KEY = 256
MAX_VAL = 512

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"", b"a", b"\x00", b"\xff", b"key", b"value", b"hello", b"world",
    b"GDBM", b"NDBM", b"snapshot", b"metadata", b"\n", b"\r\n", b"\t",
]

BOUNDARY_SIZES = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 512]

def rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))

def make_ascii_text(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-./:@\n\t"
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def make_utf8(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Construct valid UTF-8 bytes; avoid surrogate code points
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) < n:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.7:
            out.append(rng.randrange(0x20, 0x7F))
        elif choice < 0.85:
            cp = rng.randrange(0x80, 0x7FF + 1)
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
        elif choice < 0.97:
            # Avoid surrogate range 0xD800–0xDFFF
            cp = rng.randrange(0x800, 0x10000)
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                cp = 0xE000 + (cp - 0xD800)  # map into private-use area
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
        else:
            cp = rng.randrange(0x10000, 0x110000)
            out += chr(cp).encode('utf-8')
        if len(out) > n:
            del out[n:]
            break
    return bytes(out)

def make_repeated(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    b = rng.randrange(256)
    return bytes([b]) * n

def make_structured(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Simple TLV-like layout with small lengths to fit target size
    out = bytearray()
    while len(out) + 4 <= n:
        t = rng.randrange(0, 8)
        max_l = min(32, n - len(out) - 4)
        l = rng.randrange(0, max(1, max_l + 1))
        out += struct.pack('>HB', t, l)
        out += b'\x00'  # flags
        out += rand_bytes(rng, l)
    rem = n - len(out)
    if rem > 0:
        out += rand_bytes(rng, rem)
    return bytes(out)

def choose_size(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> int:
    options = [s for s in BOUNDARY_SIZES if s <= max_len]
    weights = [5.0] * len(options)
    if options:
        weights[-1] += 10.0
    extras = [rng.randrange(0, max_len + 1) for _ in range(6)]
    options.extend(extras)
    weights.extend([1.0] * len(extras))
    size = rng.choices(options, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    return size

def make_blob(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = choose_size(rng, max_len)
    if n == 0:
        return b""
    gens = [
        lambda: rand_bytes(rng, n),
        lambda: make_ascii_text(rng, n),
        lambda: make_utf8(rng, n),
        lambda: make_repeated(rng, n),
        lambda: make_structured(rng, n),
    ]
    weights = [
        3.0 if n >= 32 else 1.0,  # random
        2.0 if n <= 128 else 0.5, # ascii
        1.0 if n <= 512 else 0.5, # utf8
        2.5 if n <= 32 else 0.8,  # repeated
        2.5 if n >= 16 else 0.5,  # structured
    ]
    gen = rng.choices(gens, weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    blob = gen()
    if len(blob) >= 4 and rng.random() < 0.2:
        prefix = rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
        suffix = rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS)
        space = max(0, n - len(prefix) - len(suffix))
        core = blob[:space]
        blob = (prefix + core + suffix)[:n]
    return blob

def pack_entry(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(payload) > 0xFFFF:
        payload = payload[:0xFFFF]
    return struct.pack('>H', len(payload)) + payload

def build_entries(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    entries: List[bytes] = []
    key1 = make_blob(rng, MAX_KEY)
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.1:
        key1 = b""
    elif roll < 0.2:
        ktmp = make_blob(rng, MAX_KEY)
        key1 = ktmp.ljust(MAX_KEY, b"K")[:MAX_KEY]

    val1 = make_blob(rng, MAX_VAL)
    rollv = rng.random()
    if rollv < 0.1:
        val1 = b""
    elif rollv < 0.2:
        vtmp = make_blob(rng, MAX_VAL)
        val1 = vtmp.ljust(MAX_VAL, b"V")[:MAX_VAL]

    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        key2 = key1
    else:
        key2 = make_blob(rng, MAX_KEY)

    entries.append(pack_entry(key1))
    entries.append(pack_entry(val1))
    entries.append(pack_entry(key2))

    extra_count = rng.randrange(0, 5)
    for i in range(extra_count):
        maxlen = MAX_VAL if (i % 2) else MAX_KEY
        entries.append(pack_entry(make_blob(rng, maxlen)))
    return entries


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    entries = build_entries(rng)
    out = b"".join(entries)
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return out

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a single bytes buffer intended to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# for the gdbm_failure_atomic stub, which calls gdbm_failure_atomic(dbf, s1, s2).
# The stub requires two valid null-terminated C strings. FUZZ framework will
# split/consume the provided buffer as needed; we therefore encode multiple
# interesting text strings separated by NUL (\0). Each string is human-readable
# ASCII/UTF-8 text without embedded NUL and terminated by a NUL so that the
# fuzzer can hand them directly to c_str().
#
# We attempt to cover different semantic varieties that may trigger differing
# behaviors inside the library (paths, flags, keywords, long strings, unicode,
# edge-length strings, environment-like values, etc.).

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "

def _rand_word(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid NUL; rest is fine.
    return ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLE.replace('\x00','')) for _ in range(n))

def _path_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate Unix-like and Windows-like paths
    kinds = []
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # Unix
        parts = ["/"]
        depth = r.randint(0, 5)
        for _ in range(depth):
            parts.append(_rand_word(r, 1, 8))
        fname = _rand_word(r, 1, 10)
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            ext = r.choice([".gdbm", ".db", ".dump", ".txt", ""])
        else:
            ext = ""
        return "/" + "/".join([p for p in parts[1:] if p]) + ("/" if depth and r.random()<0.2 else "") + fname + ext
    else:
        # Windows-like
        drive = r.choice(list("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"))
        parts = [drive + ":\\"]
        depth = r.randint(0, 4)
        for _ in range(depth):
            parts.append(_rand_word(r, 1, 8))
        fname = _rand_word(r, 1, 10)
        ext = r.choice([".GDBM", ".DB", ".DMP", ""])
        return parts[0] + "\\".join([p for p in parts[1:] if p] + [fname]) + ext

def _keyword_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice([
        "atomic", "begin", "commit", "rollback", "checkpoint", "recover",
        "numsync=1", "numsync=2", "preread=1", "sync", "nockpt",
        "flags=writer", "flags=reader", "convert", "format=binary", "format=ascii",
    ])

def _env_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    keys = ["TMPDIR", "HOME", "USER", "PATH", "GDBM_SNAPSHOT", "GDBM_DUMP_FMT", "LANG"]
    vals = [
        _path_like(r),
        "/tmp",
        _rand_word(r, 3, 10),
        "/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin",
        _path_like(r),
        r.choice(["binary", "ascii"]),
        r.choice(["C", "en_US.UTF-8", "ru_RU.UTF-8"]),
    ]
    k = r.choice(keys)
    v = r.choice(vals)
    return f"{k}={v}"

def _unicode_text(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=40) -> str:
    # Include some multibyte UTF-8 characters (no NUL)
    samples = [
        "αβγδεζηθ", "漢字仮名", "пример", "exposé", "naïve", "mañana",
        "δοκιμή", "测试", "テスト", "테스트", "🙂🙃✔️❌", "ключ", "значение",
    ]
    base = r.choice(samples)
    # Optionally mix ASCII
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        base = base + " " + _rand_word(r, 1, 10)
    if len(base) > max_len:
        base = base[:max_len]
    return base

def _repeat_char(r: random.Random) -> str:
    ch = r.choice(list("-_:=,.;@#%+ "))
    n = r.randint(0, 256)
    return ch * n

def _long_text(r: random.Random, target=512) -> str:
    parts: List[str] = []
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target:
        parts.append(_rand_word(r, 3, 12))
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            parts.append(r.choice([" ", ",", ";", ":", "/", "-", "_"]))
    s = ''.join(parts)
    return s[:target]

def _snapshot_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Names resembling snapshot files that gdbm_latest_snapshot might see
    base = r.choice(["db", "store", "gdbm", "data"]) + r.choice([".snap", ".snapshot", ".bak", ".tmp"]) 
    suffix = r.choice(["", ".1", ".2", ".old", ".new"])
    return base + suffix

def _pairs_for_failure_atomic(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Build a pool of strings; fuzzer stub will request two strings per call.
    pool: List[str] = []
    # Common path-like inputs
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        pool.append(_path_like(r))
    # Keywords / flags
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        pool.append(_keyword_like(r))
    # Env-like
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        pool.append(_env_like(r))
    # Unicode
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        pool.append(_unicode_text(r))
    # Snapshot-like
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        pool.append(_snapshot_name(r))
    # Empty and very short strings (edge cases but valid as C-strings)
    pool.append("")
    pool.append(r.choice([".", "..", "/", "~"]))
    # Repeated separators
    pool.append(_repeat_char(r))
    # Longish text to test internal buffers
    pool.append(_long_text(r, target=r.randint(64, 512)))
    # Random words
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 8)):
        pool.append(_rand_word(r, 1, 24))
    # Ensure no embedded NULs
    pool = [s.replace("\x00", "") for s in pool]
    return pool

def _encode_cstrs(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Encode as UTF-8 and NUL-terminate each string; separate by NUL too.
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        out += b + b"\x00"
        if len(out) >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    pool = _pairs_for_failure_atomic(r)
    # Shuffle to increase variety across seeds
    r.shuffle(pool)
    # Limit how many strings we include to stay under 4096 bytes
    buf = _encode_cstrs(pool)
    if not buf:
        # Fallback: two simple C-strings
        return b"alpha\x00beta\x00"
    return buf

import io, os, random, struct, time
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for GDBM dump files (either ASCII or Binary format) that are valid inputs
# for gdbm_import, gdbm_import_from_file, gdbm_load, gdbm_load_from_file, and
# gdbm_load_from_file_ext. We aim to create small yet valid dumps containing
# multiple records and optional metadata to exercise different code paths.

# We implement two formats:
# - ASCII dump: a simple, line-oriented textual format commonly used by gdbmtool
#   resembling key/value entries with sizes and hex payloads. We craft a conservative
#   variant that typical importers accept.
# - Binary dump: a self-contained header + records with sizes and payload bytes.
#   We craft a minimalistic, self-consistent structure recognizable by importers.
#
# Since exact on-disk dump specs may vary across versions, we keep the formats
# internally consistent, use sane sizes, and include metadata-like fields to
# increase acceptance and exercise code paths.

# Notes:
# - We cap output size to <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic randomness based on seed.

# Helper: hex encoding grouped

def _hexbytes(b: bytes) -> str:
    return ''.join(f"{x:02x}" for x in b)

# Create diverse key/value pairs

def _make_kv_pairs(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]]:
    pairs = []
    n = rng.randint(1, 8)
    # Ensure total size under budget
    for i in range(n):
        # Choose key patterns
        kind = rng.choice([
            'ascii', 'utf8', 'binary', 'empty' if i == 0 else 'ascii', 'path', 'long'
        ])
        if kind == 'empty':
            k = b''
        elif kind == 'ascii':
            base = rng.choice([b'key', b'name', b'id', b'alpha', b'k'])
            num = rng.randint(0, 9999)
            k = base + str(num).encode('ascii')
        elif kind == 'path':
            parts = [rng.choice(['var', 'tmp', 'home', 'data', 'etc']) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3))]
            k = ('/' + '/'.join(parts) + '/' + str(rng.randint(0, 9999))).encode('utf-8')
        elif kind == 'utf8':
            # Some simple UTF-8 characters
            chars = ['α', 'β', 'γ', 'δ', '€', '雪', '🗃']
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)))
            k = ("u" + s + str(rng.randint(0, 100))).encode('utf-8')
        elif kind == 'long':
            ln = rng.randint(16, 64)
            k = b'K' * ln
        else:  # binary
            ln = rng.randint(1, 16)
            k = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(ln))
        # Value patterns
        vkind = rng.choice(['text', 'json', 'bin', 'num', 'zero', 'repeat'])
        if vkind == 'text':
            words = ['lorem', 'ipsum', 'dolor', 'sit', 'amet', 'db', 'gdbm']
            s = ' '.join(rng.choice(words) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)))
            v = s.encode('utf-8')
        elif vkind == 'json':
            obj = {
                't': rng.choice(['a', 'b', 'c']),
                'n': rng.randint(0, 100000),
                'ok': bool(rng.getrandbits(1))
            }
            v = ("{" + f"\"t\":\"{obj['t']}\",\"n\":{obj['n']},\"ok\":{str(obj['ok']).lower()}" + "}").encode('utf-8')
        elif vkind == 'bin':
            ln = rng.randint(0, 64)
            v = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(ln))
        elif vkind == 'num':
            nums = [rng.randint(0, 2**32 - 1) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))]
            v = b''.join(struct.pack('>I', x) for x in nums)
        elif vkind == 'zero':
            v = b'\x00' * rng.randint(0, 32)
        else:
            bch = rng.choice([b'A', b'\xFF', b'\x00', b'Z'])
            v = bch * rng.randint(1, 64)
        # Keep budget reasonable
        if sum(len(kk) + len(vv) for kk, vv in pairs) + len(k) + len(v) > budget:
            break
        pairs.append((k, v))
    # Ensure at least one pair
    if not pairs:
        pairs.append((b'key0', b'value0'))
    return pairs

# ASCII dump builder (conservative, self-descriptive)

def _build_ascii_dump(rng: random.Random, pairs: List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]]) -> bytes:
    # Header lines similar to gdbmtool ASCII dump style (not exact, but importer-friendly)
    lines = []
    lines.append("GDBM DUMP ASCII 1")
    ts = int(time.time())
    lines.append(f"# created {ts}")
    # Optional mode/owner metadata-like comments
    lines.append(f"# mode 0600 owner {rng.randint(0, 65535)}:{rng.randint(0, 65535)}")
    for k, v in pairs:
        ks = len(k)
        vs = len(v)
        lines.append(f"key {ks}")
        lines.append(_hexbytes(k))
        lines.append(f"value {vs}")
        lines.append(_hexbytes(v))
        lines.append(".")  # record terminator
    lines.append("END")
    data = ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode('ascii')
    return data

# Binary dump builder: simple header + records
# Layout:
#  magic: b"GDBMBDMP\0" (9 bytes)
#  version: u16 (1)
#  flags: u16 (0)
#  count: u32
#  For each record:
#    klen: u32
#    vlen: u32
#    key bytes
#    value bytes
#  trailer CRC32 over payload (optional) -> we include to increase validity feel

import zlib

def _build_binary_dump(rng: random.Random, pairs: List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]]) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    buf.write(b"GDBMBDMP\x00")
    buf.write(struct.pack('>H', 1))  # version
    # Encode a small flags bitfield: 1 = big endian, 2 = has trailer crc
    flags = 1 | 2
    buf.write(struct.pack('>H', flags))
    buf.write(struct.pack('>I', len(pairs)))
    payload_start = buf.tell()
    for k, v in pairs:
        buf.write(struct.pack('>I', len(k)))
        buf.write(struct.pack('>I', len(v)))
        if k:
            buf.write(k)
        if v:
            buf.write(v)
    payload = buf.getvalue()[payload_start:]
    crc = zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    buf.write(struct.pack('>I', crc))
    return buf.getvalue()

# Choose format and build respecting total size <= 4096

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Budget for pairs (sum of key+value) keeping header overhead in mind
    budget = 3000
    pairs = _make_kv_pairs(rng, budget)
    fmt = rng.choice(['ascii', 'binary'])
    if fmt == 'ascii':
        data = _build_ascii_dump(rng, pairs)
        # Ensure size cap; if too large, shrink pairs and rebuild
        while len(data) > 4096 and len(pairs) > 1:
            pairs = pairs[:-1]
            data = _build_ascii_dump(rng, pairs)
        # Fallback to binary if still big
        if len(data) > 4096:
            pairs = pairs[:1]
            data = _build_binary_dump(rng, pairs)
    else:
        data = _build_binary_dump(rng, pairs)
        if len(data) > 4096:
            pairs = pairs[: max(1, len(pairs)//2) ]
            data = _build_binary_dump(rng, pairs)
    # Final cap (hard trim should not occur often; but keep safety)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
